fixer.summary: combat.move() now finds the mode's MOVE_MODES entry before the Prone checks. While Prone, only modes whose spec.speed == "walk" are allowed; anything else is refused with page 186 and rule GLOSS.prone#1. A mode not in the table is also refused while Prone, as before. The double cost for crawling now uses spec.speed == "walk" instead of mode == "walk". Two unit tests were added: a Prone creature that walks pays double, and a Prone creature is refused a mode that isn't in the table. Unit tests: 362 passed. SRD and scenario tests: 329 passed, 33 xfailed. ruff check, ruff format --check and dev-gate all pass.

followups.title: dungdra/combat.py move(): crawling's doubled cost is still chosen by name (`mode == "crawl"`). Give MoveMode a field such as `crawling: bool` (or an extra-cost flag) and set it on the "crawl" entry of MOVE_MODES, so the crawl cost comes from that table like the Prone check now does.

review.summary: I'm approving this change. Both Prone checks in move() now read the MOVE_MODES table and no longer name the modes: a mode is open to a Prone creature only if it spends walking Speed. That keeps the old behaviour. Only "walk" and "crawl" spend walking Speed, and a mode missing from the table is still refused while Prone. When the creature isn't Prone, an unknown mode still falls back to walking. The refusal still cites p.186 and GLOSS.prone#1, and it carries the SRD tag. The two new unit tests check real behaviour: walking while Prone costs double and is noted as crawling, and a mode not in the table (burrow) is refused with the page and rule cited and the creature doesn't move. There's no scope creep; the costs.jsonl line is loop bookkeeping. The `mode == "crawl"` check for the doubled cost still uses the mode's name. The ticket didn't cover that check, so I've filed it as a follow-up instead of a finding.
